sources.title: Michael Aung-Thwin: Myanmar in the Fifteenth Century
sources.note: University of Hawai‘i Press description used only for the overview and short override summary: Pagan’s political decline, several successor centers, and the rise of inland Ava and maritime Pegu.

sources.title: A tale of two kingdoms: Ava and Pegu in the fifteenth century
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Journal of Southeast Asian Studies synthesis used for Ava and Pegu chronology and the upstream agrarian versus downstream commercial relationship.

sources.title: Richard M. Cooler: Introduction to the Art and Culture of Burma
sources.note: Northern Illinois University art-history text used for the limited reach of the Mongol incursions, the political collapse, river transport, and irrigated dry-zone rice.

sources.title: Aye Chan: Burma, Shan Domination in the Ava Period (c. AD 1310 to 1555)
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Journal of the Siam Society study used for the 1297 Myinsaing takeover, the 1301 siege and withdrawal, and the breakup of Pagan authority into successor centers.

sources.title: Than Tun: History of Burma, A.D. 1300 to 1400
sources.note: Inscription-based Journal of the Burma Research Society article, checked in the cached scan on printed pages 119 to 120 and 128 to 132, used for the 1297 ceremony and selected fourteenth-century food, famine and repair evidence.

sources.title: Hla Pe: Observations on Indigenous Sources for Burmese History
sources.note: Cambridge/ISEAS chapter used for the Myinsaing to Sagaing to Pinya and Ava chronological divisions and for the elite, dedicatory bias of surviving inscriptions.

sources.title: Buddhist Art of Myanmar: After Pagan
sources.note: Asia Society/Yale catalogue, especially printed pages 65 to 69, used for Bagan’s continued sacred role, Ava and Hanthawaddy art, Dhammazedi, trade goods and period-aware evidence limits.

sources.title: A Faultless Science: Dandin and Dharmadasa in Burma and Bengal
sources.note: Oxford Academic chapter used for the 1442 Pagan monastery inscription: the court-related donor couple, sale of the consort’s hair, several hundred donated texts, and works on grammar, poetics, medicine and other sciences.

sources.title: Mabel Haynes Bode: The Pali Literature of Burma
sources.note: Pali Text Society monograph used for the 1442 Pagan library donation, its royal donor couple, and its catalogued works on grammar, poetics, medicine and other branches of learning.

sources.title: The Kalyānī inscriptions of King Dhammaceti: 1892 text and translation
sources.note: Public-domain Government Printing edition used for the exact Pali opening and translation, the 1476 setting, novice literacy rules and the mission of twenty-two senior monks to Sri Lanka.

sources.title: Buddhist-Inflected Sovereignties across the Indian Ocean
sources.note: Open-access University of Hawai‘i Press scholarship used for the Kalyānī stones’ manuscript and stone-fragment validation, Haṃsavatī’s maritime links, and the Pali/Mon inscriptional context.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
sources.note: World Heritage record used for continuing worship, merit-making, farming, living communities and the layered sacred landscape; modern continuity is not treated as proof of unchanged medieval government.

sources.title: UNESCO Bagan World Heritage nomination text
sources.note: State Party nomination published by UNESCO used for the explicit archaeological limits at Bagan and evidence that Otein Taung supplied fourteenth-century inhabitants with household utensils, roof tiles and well linings.

sources.title: The Origins of Bagan: New Dates and Old Inhabitants
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Asian Perspectives article used narrowly for the tentative interpretation of vertically stacked earthenware tubes as latrine linings and the absence of a secure target-period date.

sources.title: NUS Museum: From the Ashes, Reviving Myanmar Celadon Ceramics
sources.note: National University of Singapore Museum publication used for fifteenth-century Twante kiln technology, forms, river transport, huge production and far-reaching ceramic finds, with its dating cautions preserved.

sources.title: Myo Thant Tyn and Thaw Kaung: Myanmar Historic Earthenware
sources.note: Scholarly archaeological survey used for the 1362 dated glazed jar, kiln furniture, evolving production technology and glazed wares at fifteenth-century Mrauk U.

sources.title: Richard M. Cooler: The Post Pagan Period, Part 1
sources.note: Northern Illinois University art-history text used for Ava’s location by the Kyaukse rice zone and for the qualified evidence of paintings showing station-marked dress and everyday work.

sources.title: Preliminary Analysis of Earthenware Production from Shwe Creek
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Journal of the Siam Society article used for standardized utilitarian pottery and the authors’ cautious models of attached and market production in eleventh- to fourteenth-century Bagan.

sources.title: Myanmar Ministry of Health: Milestones of Traditional Medicine
sources.note: Government historical survey used alongside the 1442 inscription study for the narrow fact that Ava-era medicinal and astronomical treatises were recorded; it is not used to invent specific treatments or access.

sources.title: Than Tun: The Royal Orders of Burma, A.D. 1598 to 1885, Part Two
sources.note: Scholarly compilation used only for its introductory chronology of Old Mon inscriptions recording Queen Shin Sawbu’s 1455 land donation and 1469 joint repairs with Dhammazedi.

proposedOverrides.summary: A broad atlas umbrella outlives Pagan’s 1297 political end and covers several successor kingdoms; Bagan’s sacred and community life continued.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id pagan-1279 is indexed circa 1279 to 1492 and occurs in the 1279, 1300 and 1400 snapshots. It is absent at 1200 and at the 1492 endpoint seam.

The 1279 and 1300 features are the same 72-position Polygon with coordinate hash e35027568fbae9667c146ca1904f4fa442f45033f58e65fae3b4fe19ecfbab0e. The 1400 version still has 72 positions and differs only slightly, with hash 4bdfa26ae5d77ae0aabe3828d71aa923b7f3e7e2d1b7917025cb3a56b3dc2c47.

All three target geometries contain Bagan, Kyaukse, Myinsaing, Pinya, Sagaing, Ava, Tagaung, Bhamo, Taungoo, Pegu, Martaban, Mrauk U, Chittagong, Yangon and Mong Mao, but not Chiang Mai. This is far broader than any defensible continuous Pagan sovereignty.

The historical Pagan royal state ended conventionally in 1297. Myinsaing, Pinya, Sagaing, Ava, Hanthawaddy-Pegu, Mrauk U and other polities are narrated as successors or neighbors, not relabelled as one Pagan empire.

The separately indexed pagan and bagan records already have cards for earlier intervals. They remain distinct; no appliesTo alias is added. A separate pegu id begins at the 1492 seam and is not absorbed into this card.
All bounds, hashes and point tests describe imported display geometry only; none establishes sovereignty, ethnicity, language, migration or modern territorial claims.
